commit.message:
refactor(tutorial): use std::copy_n instead of memcpy and raw buffer indexing

Chapters 3, 4 and 5 still wrote the message through a raw char pointer
(memcpy plus buf[n] = '\0'), which clang-tidy reports as
cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-pointer-arithmetic. Use the same
std::copy_n pattern as the other chapters, which operates on the sample
array itself, and log the message string instead of the raw buffer.
README literalinclude ranges are adjusted.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
refactor(tutorial): use std::copy_n instead of memcpy in chapter 3-5 providers (#1336)

Fixes `cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-pointer-arithmetic` (e.g.
code-scanning alert 6660) in the tutorial providers of chapters 3, 4 and
5. They still wrote the message via `memcpy` into a raw `char*` and
`buf[n] = '\0'`. They now use the same `std::copy_n` pattern on the
sample `std::array` as chapters 1, 2, 6, 10 and 12 (no raw pointer, no
`<cstring>` call). The "sent" log line prints `message` instead of the
raw buffer. README `literalinclude` ranges for these providers are
adjusted.

Verified: `--config=ci` build of chapters 3/4/5, clang-tidy aspect clean
for the three providers.
